introHeading: The roaming booth for Williamsburg's rooftop bars and loft parties
introParas: A lot of the rooftop bars and loft venues we work in across Williamsburg have one thing in common: not much room to spare. A rooftop deck along Wythe or Kent is usually built for the bar, the lounge seating and the view, not a 10ft x 10ft photo booth footprint, and a Berry Street loft floor is often already split between the DJ, the dance floor and a bar setup before anyone thinks about where a booth would go. The roaming photo booth solves that by not needing a spot at all — an attendant carries a handheld, lit capture system through the crowd, so guests get photographed wherever they already are.

It's also the easiest booth to move when a Williamsburg event does — a rooftop cocktail hour that transitions into an indoor after-party down a Berry Street freight elevator, for instance. There's no equipment to break down and rebuild; the attendant just walks the handheld system down with the crowd and keeps shooting on the other side. Sessions take under a minute, guests choose stills, GIFs or boomerangs, and the photo lands on their phone by text or email before they've moved on to the next conversation.

For a wedding or milestone birthday with a bigger guest list, we usually pair the roamer with the mirror booth — the mirror anchors one corner of the loft and draws the crowd that wants to line up for it, while the roamer covers the rooftop, the bar and the tables the line never reaches. There is no travel fee anywhere in Williamsburg — it's minutes from us, quoted from your venue ZIP code before you book.

faqHeading: Roaming Photo Booth in Williamsburg — FAQ

faqs.q: Does the roaming booth work on a small Williamsburg rooftop bar?
faqs.a: It's one of the best fits we have for exactly that kind of space. Because there's no footprint to plan around, it works on a rooftop deck that couldn't fit a static booth at all.

faqs.q: Our event moves from a rooftop to an indoor after-party — can the roamer follow?
faqs.a: Yes, and it's one of the easiest booths to move. There's no equipment to break down and rebuild — the attendant carries the handheld system with the crowd, whether that's down a Berry Street freight elevator or just to a different floor.

faqs.q: Is the roaming booth enough on its own for a bigger Williamsburg wedding or party?
faqs.a: For guest lists over about 150, we usually recommend pairing it with the mirror booth, which anchors one spot in the room and draws its own line while the roamer covers the rest of the space.

faqs.q: Do you charge a travel fee in Williamsburg?
faqs.a: No — Williamsburg is minutes from us. We quote everything from your venue ZIP code before you book.

faqs.q: Does the roaming booth need power or floor space at the venue?
faqs.a: No. The handheld capture system needs no dedicated outlet and no footprint, which is exactly why it works at Williamsburg rooftop bars and loft venues where every square foot is already spoken for.

faqs.q: Does the roaming booth print photos?
faqs.a: It's digital-first — photos go straight to guests' phones by text or email. Pair it with a static booth and printer station if you want prints too.

faqs.q: Is an attendant included with the roaming booth rental?
faqs.a: Yes. A trained attendant carries the capture system through the crowd for the full length of your Williamsburg rental.

faqs.q: Do you carry insurance and can you provide a COI for our venue?
faqs.a: Yes. We carry a $3 million insurance policy. If your Williamsburg venue needs a certificate of insurance naming them as additionally insured, reply to your booking confirmation with their contact email and we'll send it over.

faqs.q: Is the roaming booth good for a Williamsburg corporate happy hour?
faqs.a: Yes — it's a regular booking for brand activations and office happy hours at the breweries and event spaces around North and South Williamsburg, where guests are circulating rather than queuing.

faqs.q: Which Williamsburg neighborhoods do you cover?
faqs.a: North Williamsburg, South Williamsburg, East Williamsburg, Wythe Avenue, Berry Street, Kent Avenue and the surrounding areas most weekends of the season. If your venue isn't on that list, ask anyway — we'll tell you honestly whether we can get there.
